To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a series of cinnamic acid‐derived compounds as potent HDAC inhibitors, with a preference for class I HDACs.

we identified four series of HDAC inhibitors, which were found to have potent and selective activity against HDAC1 and HDAC4, and to induce apoptosis in U937 leukemia cancer cells and cytodifferentiation in CD11c cells.
we have identified four new series of cinnamy hydroxamate and 2‐ aminoanilide HDAC inhibitors with potent and selective activity toward class I HDAC enzymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological evaluation of novel series of c‐cinnamyl‐hydroxyamides and ‐2‐amino‐anilides as HDAC inhibitors.
the development of new HDAC inhibitors, with particular attention paid to their ability to induce apoptosis and to promote the differentiation of monocytes into mature dendritic cells.
the development of new classes of HDAC inhibitors with potential therapeutic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cinnamyl hydroxamates are potent HDAC inhibitors with a high potential as anticancer agents, while the corresponding 2‐aminoisophthalamides display a more selective activity against class I HDACs.
the hydroxamate series 1 and 4, and 2‐anilide series 2 and 4, have been identified as potent and selective HDAC inhibitors with a broad spectrum of biological activities.
2‐amidoanilides are more cytotoxic than hydroxamates, whereas hydroxamates are better inhibitors of HDACs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2‐amidophenyl moiety of the 2‐aminophenyl hydroxamate scaffold is amenable to substitution, thus providing a valuable platform for the design of novel HDAC inhibitors.
2‐amido‐2′‐cinnamylhydroxamic acids and 2′‐cinnamon‐2‐amino‐2′‐hydroxyanilides are new classes of HDAC inhibitors with potential therapeutic applications.

the cinnamyl hydroxamates 1, and to a lesser extent the cinnamamide 2, are more potent than the corresponding anilides 3 and 4, but all series display a similar pattern of HDAC inhibition, cytotoxicity, apoptosis induction, and cytodifferentiation activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cinnamyl scaffold, when properly substituted, is a valuable template for the discovery of new HDAC inhibitors with potential therapeutic application.
2‐amidoanilides are a new class of HDAC inhibitor with promising biological properties.
the cinnamyl scaffold is a valuable platform for the development of HDAC inhibitors with potential therapeutic applications.
